application_boundary: Firefox NativeMenuSupport creates its existing MenubarModelDBus when global-menu preferences and libdbusmenu are available. The actual application exports labels, hierarchy, accelerator/toggle/availability metadata and activation callbacks. No menu ELF hooks, DOM extraction or browser rebuild are added.
wayland_boundary: Firefox checks registrar name ownership, then sets its D-Bus address through org_kde_kwin_appmenu. The compositor retains metadata on the owning surface and sends it only to the authorized shell through version 19. Existing application controls and standard Wayland ownership stay separate.
native_boundary: The generic Python importer calls the existing NativeUI menu C API, backed by installed GNUstep NSMenu/NSMenuItem objects. It sends the existing D-Bus Event(clicked) method asynchronously; the browser owns command behavior. There is no widget drawing/layout/tracking or browser command shortcut table.
authentication: Resolve a unique session-bus owner, compare GetConnectionUnixProcessID with the compositor-provided window PID, and pin calls/signals to that unique owner. Wayland address metadata by itself is not D-Bus authentication.
findings: Firefox Wayland export requires both widget.gtk.global-menu.enabled and widget.gtk.global-menu.wayland.enabled, two libdbusmenu runtime libraries, a registrar name and the KDE Wayland app-menu manager. Test preferences affect only isolated profiles.
The two Debian packages were extracted under /var/tmp without installation. The public fixture name holder implements no X11 registration methods and is not a production desktop registrar.

Firefox MenubarModelDBus uses opened/closed events for popup lifecycle. Native submenu lifecycle callbacks are still required for lazy contents and correct Edit command updates; opening every submenu at initialization would substitute different behavior.

The compositor keeps an inert protocol object after surface destruction, and rejects duplicate objects on one owned surface. Metadata update/release invalidates the regular window snapshot rather than maintaining a second string cache.
Compositor frame acknowledgment can precede AppKit visibility/highlight changes. Tests must request and await a fresh NativeUI snapshot before using item geometry or releasing a highlighted leaf.
remaining: Automatic authenticated shell/window/focus association and a production registrar.
Native open/close callbacks for lazy menus and correct Edit/Undo availability; full live hierarchy/property behavior.
Keyboard routing shared with the native editor host, complete key/mnemonic/multi-chord metadata.
Window replacement, bus replacement/recovery, scaling/accessibility and the remaining browser controls/dialogs.
Chrome/Vivaldi/Firefox derivatives and complete GTK/Qt/KDE integration.
